rubric.detail: a real filing, not a rumour or a press mention.

rubric.label: Economic importance to the company
rubric.detail: is the news big relative to this company's size?

rubric.detail: RV20 — volume against its own 20-session median.

rubric.label: Repeat-buyer or ownership cluster
rubric.detail: the same holder building, disclosure after disclosure.

rubric.label: A clear dated catalyst ahead
rubric.detail: something on the calendar, not a vague hope.

Company denies knowing why it moved

rubric.detail: including a float too thin to sell into.

bands.label: the research line — confirmation still required

notes: The penalties can outweigh everything. A stock can score full marks on all five positives and still fail, because the four penalties are worth more (−14) than the five positives are (+13). Most days nothing qualifies — and that is the scanner working, not failing.
Scoring rules are fixed in the research playbook and are not changed to fit a result. Nothing here is investment advice or a prediction.

research.heading: Why GIHD is still on the radar
body: Two independent facts support continued investigation. First, first-half consolidated profit rose to EGP 8.710m from EGP 2.164m. Crossing 5% creates a live ownership cohort; it does not create an automatic buy.

research.heading: What price and trading activity said
body: GIHD closed 12 August at EGP 68.50, up 1.77%. EGP 50.61m changed hands versus a normal EGP 27.10m, or about 1.87× normal traded value. Share volume was only 1.22× its preceding-20-session median, below the required 3×. It closed 40.7% of the way from the day’s low to high, well below the preferred 75%, after rejecting EGP 76.50.

research.heading: Calculation notes
body: Profit growth: (EGP 8.710m − EGP 2.164m) ÷ EGP 2.164m = approximately +302.5%.
Traded-value comparison: EGP 50.61m ÷ EGP 27.10m normal = approximately 1.87× normal. This is a liquidity check, not the RV20 volume calculation.
Recent price move: Five sessions +14.84% · one month +38.08% · three months +67.69%.

tape.label: 12 Aug close
tape.detail: +1.77% · volume 1.22× normal · closed 41% up its range.

watching.research_summary: H1 consolidated profit rose 62.5%; the first completed response failed RV20 and high-close confirmation.

research.heading: Why EFIH is on the radar
body: First-half consolidated profit rose 62.5% to EGP 1.825bn. That is a credible earnings catalyst, so the stock remains in the ten-session earnings cohort while we wait to see whether buyers confirm it.

research.heading: What price and trading activity said
body: EFIH closed at EGP 23.57, down 0.55%. Share volume reached 2.00× its preceding-20-session median, which is better than normal but below the required 3×. The close was only 14.4% of the way from the day’s low to high, meaning sellers controlled most of the session. EGP 169.09m traded versus EGP 64.01m normal, so ordinary liquidity was adequate even though confirmation failed.

research.heading: Calculation notes
body: Traded-value comparison: EGP 169.09m ÷ EGP 64.01m normal = approximately 2.64× normal traded value.
Close-strength shortfall: Actual 14.4% versus required 75%: the close missed the preferred threshold by 60.6 percentage points.
Recent price move: Five sessions −1.38% · one month +4.99% · three months +12.24%.
Free float: 25.70% of shares were available to public investors, which is workable but still requires a live liquidity check before entry.

tape.label: 12 Aug close
tape.detail: −0.55% · volume 2.00× normal · closed 14% up its range.

watching.research_summary: H1 net profit rose 70.3%, but the first response had RV20 2.31× and 28.2% close strength. Operating bridges remain unverified.

research.heading: Why MFPC is on the radar
body: The 12 August 9:16 AM board indicators reported first-half net profit of EGP 9.904bn versus EGP 5.817bn, a 70.3% increase. That profit equals roughly 9.1% of the company’s EGP 108.99bn market value, so the headline is economically material.

research.heading: What we still do not know
body: The available filing did not yet provide the complete revenue, operating-profit and one-off bridge needed to judge earnings quality. A large net-profit increase is more dependable when it comes from repeatable operations rather than currency, investment or other non-recurring gains.

research.heading: What price and trading activity said
body: MFPC closed at EGP 38.00, up only 0.82%. Share volume reached 2.31× normal, below the required 3×, and the close finished just 28.2% of the way from low to high. EGP 139.60m traded versus EGP 57.34m normal, so liquidity was strong but buyers did not control the close.

research.heading: Calculation notes
body: Profit growth: (EGP 9.904bn − EGP 5.817bn) ÷ EGP 5.817bn = approximately +70.3%.
Profit versus market value: EGP 9.904bn ÷ EGP 108.99bn = approximately 9.1%.
Traded-value comparison: EGP 139.60m ÷ EGP 57.34m normal = approximately 2.43× normal traded value.
Recent price move: Five sessions +2.70% · one month +2.43% · three months −14.12%.

tape.label: 12 Aug close
tape.detail: +0.82% · volume 2.31× normal · closed 28% up its range.

watching.research_summary: H1 consolidated profit rose 55.5%; the first response closed at just 1.7% of its range with RV20 0.52×.

research.heading: Why NARE is on the radar
body: First-half consolidated profit rose 55.5% to EGP 65.372m. That is strong enough to keep the earnings event alive for further review, but a better profit figure does not prove that the market has started accumulating the stock.

research.heading: What happened after the result
body: NARE closed at EGP 17.53, down 3.79%, and finished only 1.7% of the way from the day’s low to its high—in plain language, almost at the low. Share volume was 0.52× normal, meaning it traded only about half its usual preceding-20-session median volume. EGP 20.85m changed hands versus EGP 41.05m normal. Buyers did not confirm the earnings news.

research.heading: Calculation notes
body: Traded-value comparison: EGP 20.85m ÷ EGP 41.05m normal = approximately 0.51× normal. The preferred minimum for this setup is EGP 40m.
Volume requirement: Actual RV20 was 0.52×. The rule needs 3.00×, so completed volume would have needed to be about 5.8 times the amount actually traded.
Closing-strength requirement: Actual 1.7% versus required 75%: price ended near the low instead of the high.
Recent price move: Five sessions +0.17% · one month −10.19% · three months +86.49%.
Free float: Only 14.54% of shares are publicly tradable. A smaller free float can magnify moves but also makes a safe exit more uncertain.

tape.label: 12 Aug close
tape.detail: −3.79% · volume 0.52× normal · closed near the day’s low.

watching.research_summary: H1 swung to profit, but the next close faded again to 1.1% of its range with RV20 0.95×.

research.heading: Why SMFR is on the radar
body: The company moved from a first-half loss of EGP 2.470m to a profit of EGP 13.797m. A loss-to-profit turn can be important, but it still needs confirmation that investors are buying the improvement rather than selling into it.

research.heading: What price and trading activity said
body: SMFR closed at EGP 264.18, down 1.04%, with share volume at 0.95× normal and close strength of only 1.1%. In plain language, volume was ordinary and price finished almost exactly at the day’s low. EGP 24.80m traded versus EGP 8.37m normal, so money turnover rose but buying pressure did not persist into the close.

research.heading: Calculation notes
body: Earnings direction: The year-on-year change was EGP 16.267m: EGP 13.797m profit minus the prior EGP 2.470m loss.
Traded-value comparison: EGP 24.80m ÷ EGP 8.37m normal = approximately 2.96× normal traded value.
Volume and close: Volume was 0.95× normal, not the required 3×. Close strength was 1.1%, not the required 75%.
Recent price move: Five sessions +12.42% · one month +28.04% · three months +27.68%.

tape.detail: −1.04% · volume 0.95× normal · closed near the day’s low.
